title.narrative: Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises to adopt new business models, technology and techniques to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative:
As a result of the New Law for SMEs (July 2020), the Governmental Agency for the Promotion of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEDA) role has become the main agency supporting SMEs and entrepreneurship development interventions in the country. MSMEDA (June 2020) as well as the National Council of Women (May – June 2021) have put in place several mechanisms to support entrepreneurship and SMEs development in the regions of Alexandria, Asyut, Cairo, Damietta, Qalyubia, Minya, and Monufia, using amongst others a value chain development approach to better serve women, youth and other vulnerable populations (refugees and host communities, as well as beneficiaries of the Hayat Karima National Programme). Moreover, MSMEDA reinforced their network of partners and business development service providers in the country in order to improve and innovate the delivery of non financial services offered to potential entrepreneurs. Because of these interventions, in April - December 2021, 1416 women and 395 men received training and support from MSMEDA and their affiliated partners to create or improve their business in 6 different gouvernorates
In June 2021, the National Council for Women (NCW), decided to institutionalize the ILO Financial education curricula as the main training tool on financial literacy for their beneficiaries.
Through these partnerships, innovative business models to support enterprises development programmes in the whole country with a focus on women, youth in rural areas and refugees or displaced communities are implemented and strengthened. In January -June 2021, ILO has supported the National Council for Women, the Ministry of Social Solidarity, the Central Bank of Egypt and the Egyptian Banking Institute to create a network of 25 trainers on financial education that will disseminate the financial education materials been developed by the ILO and adapted to the Egyptian context. In the governorates of Alexandria, Asyut, Cairo, Damietta, Qalyubia, Minya, and Monufia, between April 2020 and April 2021, ILO has strengthened the capacity of partners – MSMEDA, National Council for Women, Ministry of Youth and Sports, higher education institutions, NGOs (Small Enterprise Development Associations), and business development services providers to deliver entrepreneurship skills content based on the ILO tools Start and Improve Your Business (SIYB), GET Ahead and Financial education. These partners have further reach out and train final beneficiaries, and support enterprise creation and strengthening in those regions. 18 SIYB trainings have been conducted benefitting more than 360 beneficiaries (120 women and 240 men). ILO has reinforced the NCW to better serve women entrepreneurs in the gouvernorates of Damietta, Luxor, Greater Cairo, Qalobya and Mynia and to improve their business and financial education skills. More than 500 women have been trained and followed up using ILO training methodologies (SIYB, Get Ahead) in those gouvernorates.
ILO has supported women entrepreneurship interventions by organising several training of trainers virtually and physically. In total more than 86 trainers have been trained (32 men and 54 men) in all regions to support women entrepreneurship interventions in the countries. GET Ahead materials were updated and adapted to the Egyptian context. A refreshment training for 18 lead trainers and some active trainers was organized in May 2020.
These trainers are in the process of rolling out the updated knowledge within their network of GET Ahead.
